command: (review only -- the claim is the artifact)

assumptions: the converse half IS a theorem: Ambrose-Singer gives that nonzero curvature forces nontrivial holonomy. Only the forward implication fails, and the external audit's 'neither biconditional holds' is loose on this point

this places every cellular-sheaf result in this repository in the flat-monodromy regime -- the one the audit's Angle 3 identifies as the OPPOSITE of the Berry/Chern regime the archive's chain invokes at its first step
observed_result.question_for_the_reviewer: Is 'curvature vanishes identically on a graph' the right statement, or merely 'curvature is not defined'? Those are different and I may have chosen the more convenient one.
observed_result.statement: A nerve is a 1-complex: its cochain complex terminates at C^1, so the space of 2-cochains is zero and EVERY notion of curvature on it vanishes identically, while the holonomy around a cycle is a generic orthogonal matrix (defect 2.00 to 3.97 at fiber_dim 2,3,4,8). This is a counterexample, on this repository's own object, to the archive's 'non-trivial holonomy <=> non-trivial curvature'.

typed_remainders.comparison: a review binds a reading of an argument to a commit; it does not bind a number to a measurement, and it cannot promote this claim
